history.summary: This is a marketing listing title, not an identifiable project; the algo could not match it to any URA comps (0 appreciation txns, null cohort), so there is no reliable basis to certify the claimed value.
history.rating_rationale: The 'project_name' is a renovation-driven sales title, not a development the model could map to URA data: appreciation_txns is 0, the source is only regional_baseline (3.7%), and both psf_premium_vs_cohort and psf_cohort_txns are null. The -19.7% age-adj premium is computed against a district average with no project-level or same-size comps behind it, so it is not trustworthy as evidence of cheapness. Web search could not isolate the actual underlying D14 freehold project. Freehold is not a forward edge per v3.4. Without identifying the building and pulling its real recent transactions, I cannot certify either the cheapness or the resale liquidity. $1.49k psf for a 732sqft FH 1BR in D14 is plausible-to-fair but unremarkable. Honest call with the data available is Neutral at low confidence pending identification of the actual project.

Cheapness signal (-19.7%) rests entirely on a district baseline, not project/size comps
A heavily-renovated unit's PSF reflects reno premium, not the building's underlying market value
catalysts: Freehold tenure (value-retention only, not a forward return edge)
